TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND MEMBERS OF THE CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  ROBERT SAMARIO, FINANCE DIRECTOR

THRU:  KARINA BAÑALES, CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  REVIEW OF PROPOSED FISCAL YEAR 2024/25 GENERAL FUND
  EXPENDITURE BUDGET

DATE:  May 06, 2024

BACKGROUND:
The City is now well into the process for developing the fiscal year 2024/25 budget, which is
scheduled for adoption in late June 2024 will become effective July 1, 2024.

The City Council and Finance/Budget/Audit Committee (Committee) have already received
reports on the projected General Fund revenues, and the City Council was presented with an
overview of General Fund proposed expenditures.

The purpose of this meeting is to review with the Committee in much greater detail the
proposed General Fund expenditures. Staff will be soliciting feedback and recommendations
from the Committee, which staff will forward any recommendations to the City Council at the
May 13, 2024 Council meeting.

DISCUSSION:
Over the last couple of years, City staff has made a concerted effort to closely monitor
expenditures throughout the year and, in particular, during budget season, to better
understand the budgetary requirements of each line-item. The goal has been to continually
look for opportunities to refine the budget to align with actual and expected expenditures.
Thus, the proposed budget reflects adjustments to most line-item accounts, in many cases the
changes are not significant. In fact, outside of the items discussed below, the proposed budget
is only $661 different from the status quo budget.

The proposed General Fund budget for FY 2024/25 has increased in the following five areas:

  1. PERS Payment of Unfunded Liability ($63,217) - The fiscal year 2023/24 adopted
  budget did not budget for the $65,000 payment due this fiscal year. Council approved
  using monies in the City's Section 115 Trust account, created to accumulate funds for

  5
   pension liabilities, to reimburse the City for these costs as allowable under the
  regulations governing Section 115 Trusts.
  2. Election Expenses ($15,000) - This item is to cover the costs of the November 2024
  City election, which occurs every two years. As such, it was not included in the FY
  2023/24 adopted budget.
  3. Willdan Building Services ($15,000) - This increase is based on the expected costs in
  the current fiscal year of approximately $45,000 versus a budget of $30,000. There has
  been an increase in the number of applicants that are utilizing the expedited services
  provided by Willdan versus the County of Los Angeles Public Works Department, with
  whom the City also contracts for building services.
  4. Law Enforcement Services ($38,000) - Approximately $28,000 of the increase is based
  on expected costs in fiscal year 2023/24 of $283,000. It appears the budget of $255,000
  was incorrectly calculated. In addition, the contract is expected to increase 3.06%,
  amounting to approximately $10,000. These amounts do not reflect the 30% portion of
  the contract that is allocated to the COPs Fund.
  5. Wildlife Management & Pest Control ($14,000) - The City has a contract with Los
  Angeles County Weights & Measures (LACWM) in an amount not to exceed $25,000.
  This contract is primarily for coyote and other pest abatement but also covers other
  potential services. However, the City has historically utilized this service to a limited
  degree. The City Council recently directed staff to increase focus in this area.

In addition to the more significant changes described above, we have reduced the budget for
legal services provided by BB&K (Account 01-01-801) by $15,000. This amount was allocated
to Consulting Fee (Account 01-15-890) for inspection services provided by Onward
Engineering. The reduction in legal services is based on expected costs next fiscal year. In
addition, the City expects to need inspection services next fiscal year.

Attachment A contains all line-item expenditure accounts for the General Fund, including the
changes relative to the status quo budget.

FISCAL IMPACT:
None.

RECOMMENDATION:
That the Finance/Budget/Audit Committee provide feedback and recommendations to staff
based on the Committee's review of the proposed General Fund budget.
